formulas.formula: Paid twice a month? Know exactly which bills each paycheck has to cover.
1. Setup: the year, your two paydays each month (like the 15th and the last day), what happens when payday lands on a weekend, your usual take-home pay per paycheck and what's in checking now.
2. Plan what each paycheck covers for spending and savings.
3. Bills: every monthly bill with its amount and due day (1 to 31).
4. Paycheck Planner: each payday shows the bills due before the next payday, your plan, and what's left. Type your real pay in Actual Pay.
5. Watch Running Balance: if it goes red, one paycheck is carrying too many bills. Move a due date or save from the other check.
6. Spending: log what you spend. Each purchase counts toward the paycheck it falls in.
7. Monthly and Dashboard: 1st vs 2nd paycheck each month, this paycheck, and the next bills due.
A bill counts from your payday up to the day before your next payday.
Most employers pay the Friday before a weekend payday. Pick what yours does on Setup.
Type 31 for 'the last day of the month'. Shorter months use their last day.
Pick any date in Today's date on Setup to see that paycheck on the Dashboard. Blank = today.
Clear the white cells on Bills, Paycheck Planner (Actual Pay and Notes) and Spending, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Yellow: this paycheck, or a payday moved for a weekend.
Red: short this paycheck, or something to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Two paychecks, one plan.

="Paycheck "&$R$4&" of 24: payday "&TEXT(INDEX('Paycheck Planner'!$C$9:$C$32,$R$4),"dddd, mmmm d")&IF('Setup'!$R$9<'Paycheck Planner'!$C$9," (coming up)","")&". Next payday: "&TEXT(INDEX('Paycheck Planner'!$O$9:$O$32,$R$4),"dddd, mmmm d")&"."
The basics. Everything else uses these.
Like 15 or 31. Type 31 for the last day of the month. Blank = 31.
If payday falls on a weekend
Friday before, Monday after, or No change.
After tax. Change single paychecks on the Paycheck Planner.
Optional: pick a date to preview that paycheck. Blank = today.
Money in your account before the first payday.

="Paydays: the "&R11&IF(AND(MOD(R11,100)>=11,MOD(R11,100)<=13),"th",CHOOSE(MOD(R11,10)+1,"th","st","nd","rd","th","th","th","th","th","th"))&" and "&IF(R12>=31,"the last day",R12&IF(AND(MOD(R12,100)>=11,MOD(R12,100)<=13),"th",CHOOSE(MOD(R12,10)+1,"th","st","nd","rd","th","th","th","th","th","th")))&" of each month. Bills cost about "&TEXT('Bills'!C47/2,"$#,##0")&" a paycheck; your plan uses "&TEXT(C26,"$#,##0")&"."
Your monthly bills. Due day 1 to 31: days past the end of a month move to its last day.
